name: Marshall 1959RR (factory cascaded 1959 Super Lead, 100 W, 4 x EL34)
description: Marshall's FACTORY 1959RR: the Randy Rhoads 1959 Super Lead 100 W with a factory cascade, as drawn on Marshall circuit diagram 1959RR-01-60-02 Iss 2 (drawn D. Thomas 03-05-07, released 05-12-07). Built from the library's marshall-1959-plexi (Unicord 70-6-11, 1970) with every value and connection the 1959RR drawing changes, and the RR's own PSU, bias and power-stage parts. Guitar in INPUTS 2 HI (JS1; selectable): V1 pins 1-3 (R3 ∥ R4 68K, R7 100K, R2 820R / C2 330u) -> C3 22n -> VR1 'VOLUME 2' A1M -> R10 470K -> V1 pins 6-8 grid (shunted by R5 ∥ R6 68K through the empty INPUTS 1 jacks; R8 100K, R1 2K7 / C1 680n) -> C4 22n -> VR2 'VOLUME 1' A1M with C5 4n7 bright cap -> R9 470K ∥ C6 470p -> V2 pins 1-3 (R44 100K, R11 820R unbypassed) DC-coupled to the V2 cathode follower (R12 100K) -> C8 470p / R13 33K / C9 22n / C10 22n stack with VR3 B250K, VR5 A1M, VR4 B25K -> C11 22n -> 12AX7 long-tail pair (R22 82K / R25 100K, C15 47p, R17 470R, R20 10K tail, R16/R19 1M, C13 100n), global feedback R21 100K from the 4 Ω tap, presence R18 4K7 to ground and VR6 B25K rheostat + C12 100n -> C14/C16 22n, R23/R24 220K -> 4 x EL34 (5K6 grid stoppers, 1K 5W screens, R50/R51 1R cathode sense per pair; folded as two parallel-2 parts, exact) -> TX2 1.7 kΩ OT, 16 Ω tap into a 16 Ω 4x12. Supply: bridge on the HT winding (no centre tap; base two-diode equivalent), C20/C21 2 x (50u+50u) in series with R48/R49 56K balancing, choke TX3 to the screens (C22/C23 likewise with R42/R43), R27 + R26 10K 2W to the PI (C24 50u+50u), R15 10K 2W to V2 (C25), R14 10K 1W to V1 (C25). Bias: its own TX1 winding, R30 27K, D1, C18 10u (an ideal source at the C18 node, the library convention), R29 15K, C17 10u, R28 47K + PR1 20K trim. Standby closed, no master volume. Signal cut at the V2 cathode follower into the stack (as the base).

newton.note: Event substeps (docs §10.64): the tube ports of every LTE substep converge at 10x the full step's tube tolerance; every other port and the full step keep theirs. 9900X real / driven -1.3 / -2.6 %, block p99 -6.4 %; M4 Pro instructions mean / p99 -2.6 / -7.9 %. Engine fine-step truth within 0.4 %, SPICE gate within 0.001 % (abs), aliasing within 0.2 dB of 1x on both tones. CE_SUBTOL=1 restores 1x.

controls.label: Volume I
controls.note: VR2 A1M, panel 'VOLUME 1': the INPUTS 1 triode's (V1 pins 6-8) volume with C5 4n7 bright cap, feeding V2 through R9 470K ∥ C6 470p. In the cascade it is the second volume: it sets the level from the cascaded pair into V2, the PI and the power stage (the drive and loudness)

controls.label: Volume II
controls.note: VR1 A1M, panel 'VOLUME 2': the INPUTS 2 triode's (V1 pins 1-3) volume. In the 1959RR its wiper feeds the INPUTS 1 triode's grid through R10 470K, so in the cascade (guitar in INPUTS 2) it is the first volume: how hard the second triode is driven (the gain). It is silent at 0 for INPUTS 2; with the guitar in INPUTS 1 it only loads that triode's grid

controls.label: Treble
controls.note: VR3 B250K, wiper = stack output to the PI

controls.label: Middle
controls.note: VR4 B25K to ground with C10 on its wiper

controls.label: Presence
controls.note: VR6 B25K rheostat in series with C12 100n from the feedback node to ground, R18 4K7 from the feedback node to ground; clockwise shunts more treble out of the feedback

controls.label: Input
controls.note: Which HI jack the guitar is in. Input 2 (on, default): INPUTS 2 HI (JS1), the factory cascade V1 pins 1-3 -> VOLUME 2 -> R10 470K -> V1 pins 6-8 -> VOLUME 1 -> V2; the empty INPUTS 1 jacks ground their tips, so R5 ∥ R6 (34 kΩ) shunt the cascade grid. Input 1 (off): INPUTS 1 HI (JS3), one triode as on a stock 1959 high-treble channel; the empty JS1 grounds the INPUTS 2 tips. The LO jacks are empty in both. No catalogue parameter

controls.label: Bias Adjust
controls.note: CIRCUIT-ONLY factory trim (no catalogue id): PR1 20K BIAS ADJUST, the rheostat at the bottom of the R28 47K bias divider. The default is the trim position the bias winding was fitted at (grids -38 V)

controls.label: Power
controls.note: No master volume or power scaling on the 1959RR; stored for presets only

controls.label: Variac
controls.note: Variac: scales the mains (the HT and the bias winding) from 75 % at 0 through nominal at 0.5 to 108 % at 1 (as the base 1959 netlist)
controls.modNote: Not on the original amplifier: a variac on the mains. Offered as a mod; at 0.5 the amp sees its rated mains.

controls.label: Sag
controls.note: Stored for presets; sag emerges from the silicon bridge, reservoir, choke and droppers

controls.label: Response
controls.note: No part in the 1959RR circuit; stored for preset compatibility only

controls.label: Bias
controls.note: Stored for presets. The real amp's bias is the internal PR1 20K trim, modelled as the circuit-only bias_adjust control at its fitted position (as the SVT treats its factory trims)

parts.label: HT secondary (equivalent half)
parts.note: unverified: the 1959RR drawing gives no winding voltage (mains transformer D2968, 230/220/110 V taps). Amplitude kept from the base 1959 netlist (fitted there to the 1970 chart's 453 V plates). The RR rectifies the whole HT winding in a bridge (D2-D5) with NO centre tap; modelled as the base's equivalent two-diode full-wave from anti-phase ground-referenced sources of the full-winding peak (one diode drop fewer than the bridge, absorbed by the fitted amplitude). 60 Hz kept from the base (the drawing lists 117 V and 230 V mains switches)

parts.note: unverified: 20 H kept from the base netlist (c.1967 hand-drawn Marshall value); the 1959RR drawing gives the part number only

parts.label: Dropper R26 10K 2W (to the PI node)
parts.note: R26 + R27 in series: 20 kΩ total, the base's single 20 kΩ 1 W

parts.label: Bias rectifier output (C18 node)
parts.note: unverified value, FITTED: the 1959RR's bias supply is its own TX1 winding -> R30 27K -> D1 1N4007 (cathode to R30) -> C18 10u (this node). As in the JCM800 / SLO-100 / 5150 / base 1959 netlists it is modelled as an ideal source at the filter node, because a negative-peak rectifier is not charged at the mains-crest operating point that --settle 0 and the SPICE .op use (with the winding modelled, the DC point has the EL34 grids at 0 V and 0.5 A per tube; measured). C18 sits across the source and is omitted; R30, D1 and the winding are represented by it. Value fitted so that PR1 at mid-travel puts the EL34 grids at -38 V, the base netlist's bias. Scaled by the variac with the HT

parts.label: PR1 20K Bias Adjust (rheostat to ground)
parts.note: wiper tied to the grounded end as drawn; taper not printed (a trimmer, linear assumed). 0 = 20 kΩ (grids -39.2 V, coldest), 0.5 = 10 kΩ (-38.0 V), 1 = 0 Ω (-36.4 V, hottest), with the fitted -48 V source

parts.label: Output transformer TX2 (C2668): 1.7 kΩ to 16 Ω with 8 Ω and 4 Ω taps
parts.note: secondary as two series windings: ground to the 4 Ω tap (t4) and the 4 Ω tap to the 16 Ω end (spk), half the 16 Ω turns each (tap voltage ∝ √Z: the 4 Ω tap sits at half the 16 Ω tap). The 8 Ω tap carries nothing here and is not a node. Centre tap on the reservoir (before the choke) as drawn. unverified: the drawing gives the part number only; 1.7 kΩ plate-to-plate, DCRs, leakage, lm and lsat kept from the base netlist. SW4 (impedance selector, drawn at 8) is set to 16 for the 16 Ω cab. Secondary phased so the feedback is negative
